name: Solberg-Maru Electrical Systems Crew Day Rig
description: Solberg-Maru's electrical infrastructure crews are among the most aug-heavy workforces in the Circuit tier — chrome arms and neural-linked diagnostic ports are practically standard issue after three years on the job. This rig is designed around that reality. The primary garment is a flame-resistant work shirt in slate blue, rated for arc-flash exposure, with Solberg-Maru's double-helix-and-bolt logo embroidered in silver on the right chest and the worker's name patch in white on the left. The shirt has aug-accommodation construction along both sleeves: the inner seam runs on a magnetic-snap track that opens fully from shoulder to cuff, allowing a chrome arm to clear without the shirt being removed. A voltage-rated insulated over-vest in charcoal goes over the shirt — padded chest and back panels, flat front zip, and a broad rear pocket that accommodates a personal arc-flash shield in rolled form. The trousers are Fenmark ToughSeam-style in slate blue to match, with built-in knee pads, multiple tool pockets, and a reinforced gusset. Boots are Penrose Weld-style: broad-toe, steel-cap, dielectric-rated, with a side-zip for speed. A hard hat in Solberg-Maru yellow clips to the vest's back ring when not worn, and a pair of voltage-rated gauntlet gloves hang from a D-ring on the left hip. The ensemble is completed by a slim-profile BCI port cover in matte black — a snap-on shield that protects the worker's neural port from electrical field interference on high-voltage sites.
functionality: Arc-flash rated flame-resistant shell, magnetic-snap aug-accommodation sleeve seams for chrome arm clearance, voltage-rated insulated over-vest with arc shield storage, dielectric-rated steel-toe boots, BCI port interference shield for high-voltage environments, tool pockets, knee pads
what_it_says: The magnetic-snap sleeve seams say everything about who this outfit is made for: half the crew running live circuits through the district's infrastructure corridor is running chrome. Solberg-Maru built the accommodation into the uniform because it was cheaper than losing workers who couldn't get their sleeves off fast enough in an emergency. The BCI port cover is the detail that marks a veteran — newcomers forget it until the first time a high-voltage proximity alarm fires through their neural link.
manufacturer: Solberg-Maru Infrastructure Division (shirt, vest, hard hat), Penrose Workwear (boots), Fenmark (trousers)
price_range: Φ320–Φ440 (company-subsidized; worker contributes Φ80–Φ120 for aug-specific components)
story_hooks: A Solberg-Maru electrician's BCI port cover has been modified to include a passive signal recorder — someone on the crew has been harvesting electromagnetic data from high-security grid nodes without understanding what the data is worth.

The magnetic-snap sleeve seam on a veteran worker's shirt has been re-sewn in a different thread color — the original seam was cut during an incident the company's incident report describes very differently than the worker does.

A new crew member is issued a shirt with someone else's name patch still attached beneath a fresh one — the previous owner's last shift log is still accessible through the shirt's embedded RFID work-tracker.

physical_description.visual_profile: A professional electrical infrastructure worker's uniform that reads as high-spec and aug-integrated. The slate blue shirt and matching trousers create a cohesive base, layered with a charcoal insulated over-vest. The silhouette is structured and functional—broad shoulders to accommodate chrome limbs, tapered at the waist, with visible tool distribution across the body. The Solberg-Maru yellow hard hat (when worn) adds a high-visibility accent. Overall impression: a working specialist in a mid-tier corpo infrastructure division, equipped for serious electrical hazards.
physical_description.fit: Engineered compression through the torso with relaxed upper sleeves to clear augmented limbs. The trousers are straight-leg with reinforced stress points. The over-vest sits snug but not restrictive, designed for layering. Boots are broad and stable. Every element prioritizes function over aesthetic drape.
physical_description.primary_material: Flame-resistant arc-flash-rated synthetic blend (shirt), dielectric-rated insulated composite (over-vest), reinforced ballistic weave with Kevlar gusset (trousers), steel-cap boot leather with rubber/polymer soles (boots), polycarbonate shell (hard hat)
physical_description.texture: Shirt has a tight, crisp weave with a slight sheen from flame-retardant treatment. Over-vest features quilted padding on chest and back for visible structure. Trousers have a textured matte finish with reinforced seams running visibly along stress zones. Boots show industrial wear-resistance coating. Hard hat is smooth and slightly textured for grip.
physical_description.color_scheme: Slate blue (primary—shirt and trousers), charcoal (over-vest), Solberg-Maru safety yellow (hard hat and accent trim), white (name patch text), silver (embroidered logo), matte black (BCI port cover)
physical_description.closures: Magnetic-snap track along sleeve seams for aug-accommodation, flat-front zip on over-vest, side-zip on boots, snap-on BCI port cover, clip-attachment hard hat ring, D-ring carry points for gauntlets
distinctive_features: Magnetic-snap sleeve construction allowing chrome arm clarity without garment removal
Solberg-Maru double-helix-and-bolt logo in silver embroidery on right chest
Personalized white name patch on left chest
Broad rear pocket on over-vest fitted for rolled arc-flash shield
Multiple tool pockets distributed across trousers and vest
Reinforced gusset in trousers for mobility and durability
Voltage-rated gauntlet gloves on D-ring carry
Matte black snap-on BCI port cover protecting neural interface
Hard hat with back-ring clip for hands-free carry
Dielectric-rated sole and materials throughout for electrical safety
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3—working-class corpo infrastructure. Solberg-Maru is a major power-grid operator, so crew wear signals skilled labor and company affiliation, but not wealth. The aug-accommodation design reflects a company that invests in retention for experienced workers.
physical_description.cultural_context: Electrical infrastructure specialist in a mega-corp utility division. Wearing this rig signals: you've been on the job long enough to have chrome, you work high-voltage, you're trusted by Solberg-Maru, and you know electrical hazards. In the GLMZ, this is respectable Circuit-tier labor—not sub-grade salvage work, not corpo boardroom tier.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn and professionally maintained. The shirt shows minor arc-scarring and soot residue on the cuffs. The over-vest padding shows creasing from constant use. Trousers have grass stains and minor thermal scorching on the right boot area. Hard hat has faint dents and a few scratches on the visor. Everything is kept functional—patched where necessary, but not glamorous. This is gear that lives in active work zones.

image_prompt: A Tier-3 electrical infrastructure worker in full Solberg-Maru crew rig, standing in profile against a moody industrial backdrop—a high-voltage transmission tower or substation visible in soft focus behind. The worker wears the slate blue arc-flash shirt with visible magnetic-snap sleeve tracks, charcoal insulated over-vest zipped halfway, matching slate trousers with reinforced knees, and steel-cap dielectric boots. The Solberg-Maru yellow hard hat is clipped to the vest's rear ring. Their right arm is a matte-chrome cybernetic limb, the sleeve open at the magnetic snaps to showcase the arm's junction with shoulder. Voltage-rated gauntlets hang from the hip D-ring. The BCI port cover is visible as a matte black circle at the base of the skull. Moody neon-tinged lighting—blue and amber warehouse sodium lights—casts sharp shadows across the rig.
